target_behaviors: 5. Watchdog alerts only on real problems and never misses a real stall
proposed_edit: README.md owns the watchdog's live setup and heartbeat check. Apply these exact replacements. README.md, replace step 3 with: `3. Run bb automation resume $AUTOMATION_ID to start it live. After one or two checks, read the run history with bb automation runs $AUTOMATION_ID. Require a heartbeat before reporting the watchdog is live; watchdog: on, automation <id> in the run card records setup intent, not proof of a running automation. If no heartbeat appears, retry resume once and check the next run history. If it is still absent, send one normal owner status that startup did not produce a heartbeat, continue the normal orchestration loop with manual stall checks, and do not claim the watchdog is running. The heartbeat line looks like load 5 · disk 80 GB · 2 agents visible · 1/4 · OK.` SKILL.md, replace kickoff step 5 with: `5. Unless the owner said no watchdog, set it up per [README.md](README.md#watchdog): name it 🐝 <orchestrator thread title>, capture the automation id, write watchdog: on, automation <id> in the run card, pass AUTOMATION_ID, then start it live. Use the README heartbeat check before claiming it is running.` references/kickoff.md, replace section 4's watchdog bullet with: `- Unless the owner said no watchdog, follow [../README.md](../README.md#watchdog): name it 🐝 <orchestrator thread title>, capture the automation id, write watchdog: on, automation <id> in the run card, pass AUTOMATION_ID, then start it live. Use the README heartbeat check before claiming it is running.`
verification: On a disposable automation, replay the normal heartbeat path and confirm the live claim follows a heartbeat. Replay a missing-heartbeat path: confirm the automation id remains recorded, one resume retry occurs, the next history still lacks a heartbeat, a normal owner status reports that setup did not produce a heartbeat, and the orchestration loop continues with manual stall checks without claiming liveness. Confirm SKILL and kickoff point to the same README heartbeat check. Receipts are the run history, run card, and owner-facing status; no thread mutation or new service is needed.

trace_evidence.source: BB thread log and three-run watchdog alert counts
trace_evidence.observations: The thread log has no orchestrator progress events for about 6.7 hours while items were open. At the end, the owner asked 'What's the status? Why aren't agents actively working? Plz continue unless you're genuinely blocked' and the orchestrator claimed native subagents were working; the watchdog was not running. README.md currently says to inspect history after one or two checks but does not require a heartbeat before describing the watchdog as live or prescribe a response when none appears. The log does not establish which startup stage was missed; that cause remains unknown. The missed watchdog left the owner without an alert during this real stall. Across three runs, watchdog alerts were labeled 105 false, 34 real, 10 uncertain, and 21 unanswered. Those aggregate counts are context only; this proposal targets the concrete missing-watchdog path, not alert classification.
